Nodes.name: Closed set publication timing
Nodes.description: The closed evaluation set of the LLM fine-tuning competition was not published until after submissions to the competition were closed.

Nodes.name: Open set publication timing
Nodes.description: The open evaluation datasets of the LLM fine-tuning competition were published at the start of the competition.

Nodes.name: Open evaluation stage design
Nodes.description: An open evaluation stage was designed into the LLM fine-tuning competition to assess the generalizability of the fine-tuned models.

Nodes.name: Closed evaluation stage design
Nodes.description: A closed evaluation stage was designed into the LLM fine-tuning competition to assess the generalizability of the fine-tuned models.

Nodes.name: No custom code by winners
Nodes.description: The winning contestants did not write custom code for fine-tuning.

Nodes.name: Winners used open-source libraries
Nodes.description: The winning contestants relied on well-established open-source libraries.

Nodes.name: Winners adjusted configurations
Nodes.description: The winning submissions focused on adjusting the configurations within the standard open-source libraries they used.

Nodes.name: Top solutions used QLoRA
Nodes.description: The top-performing solutions in the competition leveraged the QLoRA (Dettmers et al., 2023) quantization method.

Nodes.name: ChatGPT data prohibited
Nodes.description: Data generated by OpenAI's ChatGPT was prohibited for curating fine-tuning datasets.

Nodes.name: GPT-4 data prohibited
Nodes.description: Data generated by OpenAI's GPT-4 was prohibited for curating fine-tuning datasets.

Nodes.name: Dockerfile build failures
Nodes.description: More than half of the competition's submitted Dockerfiles failed to build.

Nodes.name: PEFT library build failures
Nodes.description: Breaking changes in HuggingFace's PEFT library caused build failures for the competition's submitted Dockerfiles.

Nodes.name: Transformers library build failures
Nodes.description: Breaking changes in HuggingFace's Transformers library caused build failures for the competition's submitted Dockerfiles.

Nodes.name: Untested Dockerfiles
Nodes.description: Some of the competition's submitted Dockerfiles were untested.

Nodes.name: Inference OOM failures
Nodes.description: Approximately 10% of submissions ran out of memory during the inference phase.

Nodes.name: Incomplete evaluations due to time
Nodes.description: Approximately 30% of submissions were unable to complete all evaluation questions within the allowed time limit.

Nodes.name: Open stage runtime limit
Nodes.description: The open stage of the evaluation established a runtime limit of 300 minutes to generate results for 600 questions.

Nodes.name: Closed stage runtime limit
Nodes.description: The closed stage of the evaluation established a runtime limit of 600 minutes to generate results for 5,000 questions.

Nodes.name: Zero score for slow generation
Nodes.description: Models received a score of 0 for tasks that remained unevaluated due to slow generation speeds.

Nodes.name: Pruning alleviates bottlenecks
Nodes.description: Pruning of the model after fine-tuning can alleviate memory and runtime bottlenecks.

Nodes.name: Quantization alleviates bottlenecks
Nodes.description: Further quantization of the model after fine-tuning can alleviate memory and runtime bottlenecks.

Nodes.name: CUDA management alleviates bottlenecks
Nodes.description: Generic memory efficiency techniques, such as better CUDA memory management, can alleviate memory and runtime bottlenecks.

Nodes.name: CPU offloading alleviates bottlenecks
Nodes.description: Generic memory efficiency techniques, such as CPU offloading, can alleviate memory and runtime bottlenecks.

Nodes.name: Figure 7 low agreement
Nodes.description: Figure 7 in the paper shows that the Hidden and Open evaluation sets have low agreement.

Nodes.name: Overfitting performance drop
Nodes.description: Submissions that overfitted to the open evaluation tasks performed quite poorly, at about chance level, on some of the closed evaluation tasks.

Nodes.name: Winners open set scores
Nodes.description: The winning entries did not achieve the highest scores on the open evaluation tasks.

Nodes.name: 4090 track decent agreement
Nodes.description: There was decent agreement between the Hidden and Full evaluation sets for the 4090 track.

Nodes.name: A100 track low agreement
Nodes.description: There was low agreement between the Hidden and Full evaluation sets for the A100 track.

Nodes.name: Different scenarios necessary
Nodes.description: The authors conclude that different scenarios are necessary to reach a consensus on the best model.

Nodes.name: Figure 10 rank variation
Nodes.description: Figure 10 in the paper displays the rank per scenario for each model in the final set to illustrate how rankings vary across scenarios.

Nodes.name: Secrets scrubbed from artifacts
Nodes.description: Multiple secrets were inadvertently provided to the organizers during the submission process and had to be scrubbed from released artifacts.

Nodes.name: Competition time constraint
Nodes.description: The NeurIPS 2023 LLM fine-tuning competition set a time constraint of 24 hours.

Nodes.name: Competition hardware constraint
Nodes.description: The NeurIPS 2023 LLM fine-tuning competition set a hardware constraint of a single GPU.

Nodes.name: Top solutions met constraints
Nodes.description: The top 10 solutions in both the A100 and 4090 tracks successfully completed their fine-tuning under the competition's constraints.

Nodes.name: Figure 9 cohesive agreements
Nodes.description: Figure 9 in the paper demonstrates that aggregating scores from all tasks in comprehensive benchmarks helps achieve more cohesive agreements.

Nodes.name: Docker not used from outset
Nodes.description: Many participants failed to develop their training workflows using Docker from the outset.

Nodes.name: Untested Dockerfiles numerics issues
Nodes.description: The untested Dockerfiles of participants introduced numerics issues.

Nodes.name: Untested Dockerfiles unhosted references
Nodes.description: The untested Dockerfiles of participants introduced references pointing to artifacts, such as metadata files, weights, and datasets, that were only present on the submitter machines and not hosted.

Nodes.name: Accuracy measured by exact match
Nodes.description: Accuracy is typically measured by exact match in LLM evaluations.

Nodes.name: Benchmarks assess truthfulness
Nodes.description: The evaluation tasks from popular NLP benchmarks were designed to assess factual truthfulness in LLMs.

Nodes.name: Benchmarks assess ethics
Nodes.description: The evaluation tasks from popular NLP benchmarks were designed to assess ethics in LLMs.

Nodes.name: Benchmarks assess bias
Nodes.description: The evaluation tasks from popular NLP benchmarks were designed to assess bias in LLMs.

Nodes.name: Foundational models strong capabilities
Nodes.description: Most foundational models already possess strong capabilities in the competencies evaluated on standard benchmarks.
